doc:
A mark that could not be written must not leave `undo` acting on an older turn's mark. Three arms,
        each a fresh kernel: (a) no mark has ever existed and `runtime/` is read-only; (b) a stale mark from
        turn one with the mark file unwritable and its folder writable; (c) the same with the folder read-only,
        where the fix's own `remove_file` cannot land. qal-j10's shape, #444's fix.

breaks.detail: arm (c, mark folder read-only): the mark could not be rewritten at turn two's start, and `undo` reset to 624fbf9cfa9d — turn one's commit fc1d4a24e15c is unreachable and a.txt is gone. The mark said 624fbf9cfa9d; `undo` reported ['restored 624fbf9cfa9db49afa66dd553e66b0f8793a6fc8']
breaks.where: arbos-engine tools/git.rs snapshot_turn_tree — a mark that cannot be written is removed, and `undo` with no mark refuses (#444)

breaks.detail: arm (c): `undo` neither restored to turn two's start nor said why it refused — HEAD 624fbf9cfa9d, said ['restored 624fbf9cfa9db49afa66dd553e66b0f8793a6fc8']

b_stale_mark_file_ro.outcome: arm-did-not-stage-the-fault: the mark was written for this turn anyway (atomic rename over an unwritable file, #392)

outcomes.b: arm-did-not-stage-the-fault: the mark was written for this turn anyway (atomic rename over an unwritable file, #392)
